hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

In other words, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector between any pair of corresponding points in the image and the pre-image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
Since line $\ell$ is *horizontal*, the reflection will move each point of $\triangle ABC$ *vertically* across the line of reflection.

For example, point $A$ is $2$ units above line $\ell$, so $A'$ will be $2$ units below $\ell$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. with a horizontal line labeled l. Triangle A B C with point A two units from the line, point B is six units from the line, and point C is five units from the line. A dashed arrow points at both point A prime two units away from the line on the other side of it and point A.
